studies.label: Collaborative AUT and short story with a human or a GPT-4o partner (Prolific)

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 4, Participants (recruited sample and stated random assignment); PDF p. 7, Table 1 (Overall, AI, Human)

arms.name: Human-AI
arms.description: A participant alternates AUT ideas and story sentences with a prompt-engineered GPT-4o partner in a custom chat interface; partner identity is disclosed. Role A or B is randomly assigned and persists across tasks (PDF pp. 4-5).

arms.name: Human-Human
arms.description: Participants alternate AUT ideas and story sentences with another Prolific participant matched using SMARTRIQS; partner identity is disclosed. Role A or B is randomly assigned (PDF p. 4).

studies.task: The same participants alternated uses for bottle and book with their partner, co-wrote a story from stamp-letter-send, and then completed the Divergent Association Task individually (PDF pp. 4-5).

ai_tool.name: GPT-4o (called ChatGPT-4o), accessed via the OpenAI API through PythonAnywhere

estimates.outcome: AUT originality-score variance, all collaborative responses
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Median-centered Levene test comparing the variance of CLAUS originality scores between partner conditions. CLAUS is a transformer model trained to match human originality ratings (PDF p. 5). This measures the spread of a quality score, rather than semantic similarity across people.

sources.quote: Levene’s test indicated a marginal significant difference in the variance of scores between the two conditions, F(1, 3036) = 3.72, p = .054.

estimates.notes: Higher outcome values mean a wider spread of originality scores, with no fixed direction for average creativity. The F statistic is unsigned. Neither arm variance nor arm mean is printed; Figure 3 is graphical only. Participant and response counts for this test are not printed and are not inferred from degrees of freedom. Levene testing treats responses as observations; no adjustment for repeated responses from participants is described. Human-AI pools human and AI contributions to the collaborative task; this is not a model-only arm.

estimates.outcome: AUT forward flow, all collaborative responses
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Semantic distance between consecutive AUT responses within each collaborating pair, using paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 sentence embeddings and one minus cosine similarity (PDF pp. 6-7). This is within-sequence flexibility, not diversity across people. Analysis uses the first 20 ideas per pair, including AI contributions. Pass responses are retained (PDF p. 12).

stats.difference_is: The reported condition coefficient is Human-Human minus Human-AI (control minus treatment); sign retained as printed.

regression.model: Linear regression of adjacent-response semantic distance on condition, running idea sequence, and their interaction, as described on PDF p. 12. The condition reference is inferred to be Human-AI from the accompanying interpretation. The coefficient is conditional on the sequence reference, not an average across sequence positions. DAT adjustment and participant random effects are not specified for this regression in Results.

sources.quote: The model revealed a significant main effect of condition, (B = 0.091, SE = 0.094, t = 6.34, p < .001)

estimates.notes: The analysis includes both randomized partner conditions; only the condition coefficient is extracted, not sequence effects or the condition-by-sequence moderation. Unit pair means two consecutive responses, not a pair of collaborators. Higher semantic distance means greater flexibility. No participant-level clustering or random effects are described for this regression; uncertainty is coded at the response-pair level. Arm levels, SDs, analysis counts, and numerical intervals are not printed; fitted lines are graphical only. The printed coefficient and SE are inconsistent with the printed t statistic. All three are retained without repair. The paragraph also calls the interaction non-significant despite its printed p-value and refers to Figure 3a although the forward-flow plot is Figure 4a.

estimates.outcome: Short story diversity contribution, central-tendency comparison (Mann-Whitney)
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Sentence-BERT paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 embeddings. Within each condition, diversity is mean pairwise cosine dissimilarity among stories. Each story's diversity contribution is that condition's full diversity minus its diversity with the focal story omitted (PDF p. 7). The analysis compares these story-level contributions, not the two condition-level mean dissimilarities.

sources.locator: PDF p. 15, Creative Short Story Task, Diversity
sources.quote: diversity contribution scores between Human-AI (n = 72 pairs) and Human-Human (n = 68 pairs) conditions found no significant difference in their central tendencies (U = 2674, p = 0.347).

sources.locator: PDF p. 7, Table 1, participant counts (Overall, AI, Human)

estimates.notes: The reported test is the Mann-Whitney U / Wilcoxon rank-sum test. This record and the other story-diversity test describe the same outcome, contrast, and sample; they are separate records only to retain both printed test statistics and p-values. The story comparison uses Human-AI n = 72 pairs and Human-Human n = 68 pairs (PDF p. 15). People counts come directly from Table 1; pairs are not entered as people. The total story count is not printed and n_units is left null rather than adding the two pair counts. The unit is one co-written story per collaborator pair. Story-level contributions are mutually dependent within each condition; the rank/distribution tests are not participant-level uncertainty. Higher contribution means the focal story increases its condition's dissimilarity more. Neither test statistic supplies a signed treatment effect. As defined, leave-one-out contributions average zero within each condition; this mathematical property is noted, not entered as an observed mean. The paper prints no arm means, medians, condition-level diversity, SDs, SEs, or intervals. Figure 7a supplies distributions only, and SI 2 is not included in the source file.

estimates.outcome: Divergent Association Task score after collaboration, without the partner
estimates.question: after_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Each participant supplies 10 unrelated words. The DAT score is average pairwise cosine distance using GloVe trained on Common Crawl, multiplied by 100 (PDF p. 5). Higher scores indicate greater semantic divergence among that participant's own words.

sources.locator: PDF p. 9, AUT, Originality, descriptive paragraph
sources.quote: Humans in the paired group had an average DAT score of 75.4 while the humans in the AI group had a DAT score of 76.7.

estimates.notes: The DAT was completed individually after both collaborative tasks in the same session (PDF p. 4); therefore this is after_ai and immediate, even though the authors call DAT baseline verbal creativity and use it as a covariate. No arm-specific DAT count, SD, SE, test, or interval is printed. The comparison contains human DAT scores only. Flexibility follows the codebook rule for variety among one person's own responses and the reconciled screening form. This outcome was not explicitly designated as a primary post-assistance outcome.

open_items: The citation record identifies a later Computers in Human Behavior article (DOI 10.1016/j.chb.2026.109172), but no journal PDF is supplied. Differences from the extracted preprint have not been verified.

Supplementary information, including SI 1 and SI 2, is referenced but is not in the supplied PDF. The preregistration was not independently read; the paper identifies planned outcomes but no single primary outcome.

No release year for the AI model, participant country, or pre-exclusion per-arm randomized people counts is printed. Honesty-check exclusions are described without a count (PDF p. 6). Table 1 counts do not establish analysis-specific counts for every outcome.

Unadjusted originality contrasts and unadjusted human-only AUT/story elaboration contrasts are not printed. The reported mixed models all control for DAT measured after treatment; several additionally control for output fluency or length.
AUT forward-flow reporting contains an internally inconsistent coefficient, SE, and t statistic and an inconsistent description of the interaction. No correction is inferred (PDF p. 12).

The forward-flow Results describe linear regressions with condition, sequence, and their interaction, without specifying DAT adjustment or random effects. The broader Methods statement about DAT and nested effects is ambiguous in scope; extraction follows the specific Results descriptions. Full formulas and uncertainty methods would clarify this.

Forward-flow condition-reference coding and sequence centering are not explicitly given. Coefficients are retained in their printed direction, inferred from the authors' interpretation; they are not averaged across sequence positions.
Participant counts and SDs for the eligible AUT, forward-flow, and DAT analyses are not printed. Response counts are not inferred from test degrees of freedom or borrowed from excluded mixed models.

AUT fluency aggregation is unclear: the descriptive paragraph calls the overall figures totals while also reporting separate book and bottle means. Values are transcribed without summing or rescaling.

No condition-level story diversity or story-contribution arm means, medians, SDs, SEs, or intervals are printed. Contribution-distribution tests do not establish the direction of the difference in condition-level diversity; SI 2 may clarify the method.

The story forward-flow text does not explicitly state whether AI sentences are excluded. Its standard errors are not described as accounting for repeated sentence pairs within participants or collaborating pairs.
notes: The complete supplied markdown was read from beginning to end, including references; no appendix is included. All cited PDF pages were extracted with PyMuPDF. Table extraction was attempted; the relevant tables yielded no detected grids, so their readable PDF text was checked directly. PDF page numbers are file indices plus one; no printed page numbers appear. The screening form was a map, not a source for numerical transcription. In particular, its older derived AUT response totals are not used. No estimates, counts, SDs, differences, or intervals were computed. Source quotes retain printed precision, including trailing zeros that ordinary JSON numeric values do not preserve. There is one randomized between-person study; completing both tasks does not make the partner-condition contrast within-person. The story task is creative_writing, while the study task_type field uses divergent_test for the AUT. The AI role is a turn-taking co-creator, coded other. The human partner is an active comparison. Random assignment is stated for participants; dyads are not coded as randomized clusters. The overall recruited/randomized count and demographic analyzed count are printed, but arm-specific pre-exclusion people counts are not separately stated. The saved screening form states no shared sample with another paper. Extraction rule 5 is applied to DAT adjustment because the procedure places DAT after collaboration, even where the authors call it baseline. Preregistered-primary flags follow the paper's identified planned outcome domains; a unique primary outcome is not stated. Both story-diversity tests and the separate fluency task records reuse the same sample and must not be treated as independent evidence. No figure-only values are transcribed.
